text:
alex: heads up — ran into a weird packaging/install issue when onboarding the python sample app. poetry 1.6.0 resolver picked a wheel that doesn't include the async entrypoints, so imports fail at runtime.

alex: repro steps: `poetry add redwood-sdk[async]` on py3.11 image (ubuntu-latest)
```
Using version ^1.8.0 for redwood-sdk
Resolving dependencies... (0.9s)
  SolverProblemError
```

alex: runtime error when starting the sample: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 2, in <module>
    from redwood import AsyncClient
ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'redwood' (/workspace/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py)
```

sam: can you paste your pyproject extras and the lockfile snippet?

alex: minimal pyproject extras I used:
```
[tool.poetry.extras]
async = ["httpx[http2]", "aiofiles"]
```
I tried both `redwood-sdk[async]` and separate `redwood-async` package pins, same result.

maria: hmm — could be the resolver preferring a binary wheel built without the optional extra installed. poetry's resolver sometimes backtracks and chooses a distribution that satisfies metadata but lacks package_data for extras.

maria: quick workaround: `pip install .[async]` in the venv (pip honors extras at install time). can you try `poetry run pip install "redwood-sdk[async]==1.8.0"` and see if that loads AsyncClient?

alex: tried pip install -> that worked, AsyncClient imported. confirms it's a poetry/resolver selection issue.

tim: this sounds like the poetry 1.6 resolver bug we've seen with wheels that embed conditional package_data. there's an open GH issue: https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/issues/XXXX (cc @devex) :thinking:

devx-bot: created ticket DEVPY-412: Investigate poetry install -> missing async entrypoints for redwood-sdk (linked to sample-app onboarding).

jia: short-term DX fix: update sample-app README to recommend `python -m pip install -e .[async]` or include a pinned requirements-dev.txt produced with `pip-compile` so new users don't hit this. We should also publish a wheel that includes async code in the base package (no extras) so imports don't break if resolver drops extras.

sam: +1 on publishing a single wheel that contains AsyncClient (or providing a clear import path like `from redwood.asyncio import AsyncClient`) — that avoids relying on extras. Also add a CI step to verify the wheel artifacts on a clean py3.11 env.

maria: for immediate unblock: patch the sample app to call `from redwood import AsyncClient  # fallback for pip installs` and add a note. I'll open a tiny PR.

alex: thanks — PR landed, confirm sample-app works on CI with the pip install fallback. I'll update onboarding doc.

jia: I'll coordinate with releases to publish the compatibility wheel and add a packaging checklist item: test extras + pip + poetry resolver scenarios on 3.9/3.10/3.11.

alex: leaving this thread as the canonical repro. followups in DEVPY-412. thanks y'all! :tada:
